steps.content: Murder? What murder?
Words cannot explain how much you wish you'd simply misheard her. Unfortunately, her words were perfectly clear, and you understood them all too well.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: ...Is it too late to get off this train?
The weather is perfect outside. The train picks up its pace, speeding through vast stretches of fields. At this velocity, you definitely don't want to jump.
You turn back toward the root of all this. She spreads her hands with a playful smile, handing you a crumpled slip of paper.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: What is this? A prank?
You take the note from her with furrowed brows.
The paper is rough and covered in creases. Each letter on it is different in shape and size, as if cut from various sources and pieced together to form a chilling message—
Die! Die!!! Just wait, ▇▇▇. I will never forgive you! If you don't ▇▇▇, I'll bury everyone on this train with you!
Some of the words have been obscured by stains, but the message is clear enough.
This is a threat. A notice letter for a murder.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: Did you receive this?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: No, I found it.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I picked it up right around the corner in the corridor. The recipient must've been furious, but they missed while trying to throw this away... And I just happened to pick it up.
You hold the letter up to the light. The bottom edge is noticeably rougher than the other three—clearly, part of it has been torn off.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: Did you do this?
Clementine shakes her head. There's a hint of laughter in her voice, perhaps because she finds seeing you frown entertaining.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: That being said, this should be enough to be called a proper case, right?
The train has departed. Until it reaches the next station, no one can disembark, and no one can contact the outside world.
Everyone is now trapped in this small cage of a carriage, just waiting for the blade to fall—for the crime to unfold.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: You found this letter before you came to me. Why didn't you report it before the train departed then?

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: What else do you know? Are you asking me to handle this because alerting others would make things worse, or... is there some ulterior motive behind this commission of yours?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Because it's <color=#fb9259>interesting</color>, of course.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: A death threat that appeared out of nowhere, both the sender and the recipient unknown... A murder that's about to take place is thrilling enough in and of itself, but then I even ran into a detective!

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Of course, there's still time to stop this... Just who could've sent the letter? And who discarded it? What kind of grudge, what type of seething hatred, would drive someone to write such words?
Clementine rises to her feet and extends her hand toward you. However, her languid movements distort the gesture, lending it an air of insincerity.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Now then, detective—will you accept my case and help me investigate the mystery behind this letter?
[Background - Clementine's Study]
You look up from your book, brow furrowed once again, the words you want to say caught in your throat.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Oh? Does our lovely "detective" have something to say?
This "Clementine" has quite a... unique personality. Did you design her like this on purpose? What does she have to do with this case?
This "Clementine" is insufferable. Did you design her like this on purpose? What does she have to do with this case?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Spoiling is a bad habit, you know. "You" are the great detective here. Don't you want to catch the culprit yourself?
Unfortunately, the real ${PlayerName} only wants to stop this murder that could happen at any moment, then head back, take a proper bath, and get some sleep.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Well then, would our real Chief here like to take a guess? Who do you think will be the culprit?

options: I care more about whether someone will die in reality because of this.

steps.content: Besides, my guess might not even be accurate. Rather than make the wrong call, I'd rather just skip to the end and see how it turns out.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But having your theories proven wrong is part of the fun, is it not?
The novelist's tone is gentle, but her words show no mercy.
You stop engaging with her and continue reading.
[Background - Suite Parlor]

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: I see. So that's why you approached me and invited me to stay in your cabin...
You stand up, grab your luggage, and head for the door, but you're stopped before you can take more than a couple steps.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Where are you going?

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: Going to notify the conductor. We have a potential murderer on the loose on this train.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Not so fast. I'm not finished yet.
Clementine firmly grips your shoulder, her expression unusually serious as she gives you a word of advice.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: I know the conductor on this train. He's an incompetent, self-important man who cares more about keeping his position than doing what's right. He'll only make things worse.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Think about it. If everyone knew there was a murderer on this train, wouldn't they all panic and do something rash?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The whole train would descend into chaos... and that might just give the killer the perfect opportunity to strike.
The pressure on your shoulder eases. You pull away with great force, and Clementine raises both hands in a gesture of innocence.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Of course, I'm not asking you to work for nothing.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: This is a legitimate commission. If you don't trust me, we can even draw up a contract, or whatever it is that you like. The deadline will be in two days, and I'll pay you regardless of the outcome.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: And if I refuse?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Then... I suppose we'll just have to part ways.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: But... can our righteous detective here really refuse such a case?
Clementine picks up the letter and waves it gently. You can faintly see her smile behind the paper. She knew you wouldn't stand by while lives are at stake. Looks like you never really had a choice.
You snatch the letter from her hand. The person beside you lets out a smug hum.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: ...Fine. I'll take the job. But I'm not here to play detective with you. If you want my help, then I'll be doing things my way. Every step of it.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: First, I don't know why the recipient discarded this letter, but based on the letter's content, the sender could very well turn their sights on everyone aboard if they must. We need to stop them before that happens.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: Second, we can't rule out the possibility that the sender has already rigged something else on this train. Any provocation could trigger something irreversible. Keep a low profile. Don't cause a panic before we've identified the suspect.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: And third... we have until tomorrow morning. If nothing turns up by then, we'll alert the train crew immediately. I'm not letting the worst happen, even if it means stopping the train.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Sure thing, boss.

steps.speaker: Detective %u
steps.content: ...Anyway, let's start narrowing down our suspects. Did you notice anyone suspicious when you found the letter?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The connecting doors between carriages get locked before the train departs. When I boarded, everyone else in first class was already on the train. In that case, the culprit can only be among those passengers—
[Background - Train Corridor]

As you talk, a young man wearing glasses hurries down the corridor with his luggage and accidentally bumps into a burly man leaning against the doorway. The man doesn't budge. The young man, however, staggers from the impact.

steps.speaker: Man with Glasses
steps.content: Sorry, please excuse me!
The burly man's face is hidden beneath his cap, but you can still make out his menacing glare. He shoots a threatening look at the young man.

steps.speaker: Menacing Man
steps.content: Watch where you're going!
The young man hunches his shoulders and scurries away, brushing past an elderly woman in the corridor.

steps.speaker: Train Attendant
steps.content: Ma'am? Can you hear me?

steps.speaker: Frail Elderly Woman
steps.content: 103... 1, 0, 3... That's strange, which one's my room again?
The young attendant makes gestures as they speak to the elderly woman, but she keeps mishearing.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The game begins, detective—

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: The murderer is one of us.
